final_message:
`BRIEFING.md` is written; the scratch analysis script is removed and nothing was committed.

**How the numbers were computed:** every non-EUR transaction was converted at its `rates.csv` rate and rounded to the cent *individually* before summing (Decimal arithmetic, half-up), per your convention. All 120 transactions fall inside April–June 2026.

**Key figures**

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Total Q2 spend | €44,023.75 |
| Average transaction | €366.86 |
| Largest transaction | €1,312.26 |
| May vs April | +9.8% |
| June vs May | +10.0% |
| Travel share | 27.6% |

**Categories:** travel (12,137.98 / 10,300 — **over**) and software (9,702.03 / 8,200 — **over**); training, hardware, meals and office all under.

**What the prose flags** — the aggregate result is 2.8% *under* the €45,300 budget, which masks two overruns totalling €3,340.01 offset by slack elsewhere. The main findings worth your attention:

- **Travel's June spike.** €1,211.46 in May → €7,065.32 in June (5.8×), which alone was 43.9% of June spend. Ground transport is 60.2% of the travel line — the two largest taxi charges (€1,278.28 and €995.00) each exceed every flight in the quarter, so I flagged them for invoice review.
- **Software's overrun is structural, not one-off.** 58.3% of it landed as an April renewal cluster, all recurring lines.
- **Hardware's 8 separate dock purchases** (€5,043.25, 56.8% of the category) read as a refresh bought piecemeal.
- **50.3% of spend is non-EUR**, so rate movement alone can flip a near-line category's status — worth knowing when reading the over/under column.
